info.name: Publication Research Backend
info.description:
AIS Research Publication Site API. Imported from the live OpenAPI spec at /swagger/v1/swagger.json.

Quick start:
1. Run Auth > Login with your Admin (or any) credentials — the access/refresh tokens are saved automatically into collection variables.
2. Every other request inherits Bearer auth from the collection using {{access_token}}.
3. When the access token expires, run Auth > Refresh to get a new pair.

request.description:
Admin-only. Wipes and recreates the whole schema, then reseeds the 8 roles, the configured Admin and — where this deployment asks for it — the demonstration dataset (every account uses DevTest123!). Returns as soon as signing in is possible again; the demonstration publications are rebuilt in the background, so poll GET /api/dev/demo-data to see when it has finished.

Returns 403 unless BOTH DevTools:EnableDatabaseReset and Seed:DemoData are enabled — the second is what marks a deployment's data as disposable. Log in again afterwards; tokens issued before the reset stop working.
Admin-only. Whether this deployment carries the demonstration dataset, and how much of it is there. Answers the question the reset leaves open, since the rebuild finishes after that response.

Admin only. Every invitation and its state: pending, accepted, expired or withdrawn.

Admin only. How anyone gets an account where self-registration is closed, which is every deployment that is not a development one. The role is fixed at the moment of sending, so the person cannot choose their own. DepartmentId is required for the roles that belong to a department (Student, Supervisor, Coordinator, HeadOfDepartment) and ignored for the rest.

Returns 422 if the invitation was created but could not be emailed — the row still exists and the audit trail records it; use Resend once a mail server is configured.
Admin only. Issues a fresh token, so the previous link stops working — re-sending because an email went astray should not leave two live ways in.
Admin only. Kills the link. Refused once the invitation has been accepted: disable or delete the account instead.

No account required, by necessity — the whole point is that this person has none. The token is the only credential; it is unguessable and single-use. Tells the invited person who invited them and as what, before they set a password.
No account required. Creates the account enabled and with its address already confirmed — the invitation reaching that inbox is itself the proof the address works.
